notes:
Lead profile: small SaaS focused on help-center + chat widget (agents + bot hybrid). Early self-serve signup, used free credits to wire up quick POC. Key pain: perceived latency hurting UX — users in West Coast complain about 1-3s response spikes vs desired <500ms for simple utterances.

Call notes / shorthand: 
- "It feels snappy sometimes but then just stalls for a second or two — looks like a tail latency thing" (product mgr).
- Workload: mainly short chat queries (average prompt ~120–300 tokens including context), some doc search / embedding lookups (batch embedding jobs nightly).
- Targets: p95 <= 400ms for generation-only short prompts; bulk embedding throughput modest (50k tokens/day), cost sensitive.
- Model preference: want small/medium open models (quantized variants ok). Asked about Redwood-verified model profiles and how fallback routing would behave.
- Region choice: customer is US-west heavy (SF office + customers). SE note: recommend provisioning hosted endpoint in us-west-2 for lowest RTT; discuss cross-region fallback to us-east-1 only for capacity events.

- Prompt guidance: trim system + history where possible; keep context windows for short-turn chats to 600 tokens; for knowledge retrieval chain, do retrieval -> condense -> generate (condense step 50–120 tokens). Aggressively truncate long threads before calling generation.
- Batch & caching: enable prefix caching for repeated welcome/prompts; recommend caching embeddings for repeat queries, set cache TTL 24h.
- Observability ask: wants token-level cost/latency per route in Console; flagged need for alert if p95 > 600ms for >5 minutes.
